model: HVEA Pyramid - Windows XP variant (M57-Patents Charlie, Jo, Pat test environment)
notes: Paths reflect Windows XP SP3 conventions confirmed against M57 images (Paper II Section 4.1). User profile layout: /Documents and Settings/<name>/. Event logs as /WINDOWS/system32/config/*.evt. Recycle bin at /RECYCLER/<SID>/. Outlook Express identities under Local Settings/Application Data/Identities/{GUID}/Microsoft/Outlook Express/.

tiers.name: Attribution and Environment Anchor
tiers.function: Establishes identity and configuration context. All higher tiers rely on Tier I for interpretive stability.

tiers.name: Primary Evidentiary Object Layer
tiers.function: Contains the semantic focus of investigation: user-generated artifacts and outward interaction indicators.

tiers.name: Behavioral Contextualization
tiers.function: Bridges attribution and payload: execution chronology, application interaction, deletion residues.

tiers.name: System-Level Independent Corroboration
tiers.function: Provides structural validation independent of semantic payload interpretation.

layers.name: System & Hardware Baseline
layers.purpose: Establish the operating environment required for interpretation (OS version, file system type, disk layout, installed-program baseline, system time configuration).

layers.name: User & Machine Identity Context
layers.purpose: Defines attribution scope and identity anchoring (user accounts/SIDs, profile directories, registry system hives, group membership, machine identifiers).

layers.name: User Content (Evidentiary Payload)
layers.purpose: Recover primary evidentiary objects under identity attribution. Contains documents, media, financial records, archives, downloads.
typical_sources: My Documents, Desktop, Downloads under user profile

acquisition_paths.note: Temp content overlaps with G but documents in temp count as payload during active sessions.

layers.name: Network Interaction Presence
layers.purpose: Identify boundary-crossing activity and external interaction context. XP stores DHCP and network profile data in the SYSTEM hive (Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces, NetworkList absent in XP).

acquisition_paths.note: Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces and Services keys; co-acquired with Layer A SYSTEM hive.

layers.name: Execution & Recency Telemetry
layers.purpose: Reconstruct execution chronology linking identity to payload access. Prefetch is the primary XP source (no Amcache or Shimcache until Win7+). UserAssist key in NTUSER.DAT records executed-program counts and timestamps.

acquisition_paths.note: XP stores Recent shortcuts directly under the profile, not under AppData like later Windows.

layers.name: Browser & Application Interaction
layers.purpose: Contextualize acquisition, research, and dissemination behavior. M57 investigations show IE (index.dat), Firefox (places.sqlite, cookies.sqlite), and webmail browsing as the dominant browser footprints.
typical_sources: Outlook Express identities for webmail-adjacent artifacts

acquisition_paths.note: IE cache and index.dat. Note: NTFS may protect this directory; mount with show_sys_files.
Firefox cache lives under Local Settings; profile under Application Data.
Outlook Express identities under {GUID}/Microsoft/Outlook Express/. Contains .dbx mail stores and Pop3uidl files.

layers.name: Deletion & Transient Residues
layers.purpose: Detect deletion intent and artifact lifecycle behavior. XP uses RECYCLER not $Recycle.Bin; INFO2 file tracks deletion metadata. Temp files in profile-local Temp paths.

acquisition_paths.note: XP Recycle Bin convention: /RECYCLER/<SID>/Dc<n>.<ext> plus an INFO2 index. May persist after emptying in unallocated space.

layers.name: Event Logs (System Temporal Chronology)
layers.purpose: Independently corroborate authentication, boot, and service chronology. XP uses the legacy .evt format under WINDOWS/system32/config, not the .evtx format introduced with Vista.
typical_sources: XP event log files in system32/config

acquisition_paths.note: Catch-all for any additional .evt files (e.g. internet explorer, DNS service).

layers.name: NTFS Metadata (Structural Ground Truth)
layers.purpose: Validate file lifecycle and structural consistency independent of semantic interpretation. $MFT entries, MAC timestamps, structural attributes.

layers.name: USN Journal & File Change Chronology
layers.purpose: Reconstruct fine-grained file-system change chronology and concealment behavior. XP UsnJrnl timestamps have known parsing quirks (epoch base differs); use file-name evidence as primary signal.

acquisition_paths.note: $LogFile excluded; supports transactional crash recovery, not evidentiary chronology. XP parsing caveat documented in Jo investigation notes.

dependencies.rationale: Identity context (B) is interpreted within the operating environment baseline (A). Without A, B's SIDs and profile paths lack environmental grounding.
User content (C) requires identity attribution from B. Documents and downloads cannot be reliably associated with a specific user without B's SID and profile context.
Network interaction (D) requires attribution boundary from B to associate boundary-crossing activity with an identity.
Execution telemetry (E) links identity to payload access; the identity anchor is B.
Execution telemetry (E) is interpretively about access and handling of payload (C). Without C, E events lack semantic targets.
Browser interaction (F) requires user attribution from B; browser profiles and Outlook Express identities live under user-account paths.

Deletion residues (G) reflect post-creation handling of payload (C). G's interpretive value depends on what was deleted relative to C. M57 investigations show Jo's Pop3uidl.bak in RECYCLER as a Layer C-to-G linkage.
RECYCLER entries are SID-scoped (RECYCLER/<SID>/...); G requires B for user attribution.
Three-source convergence pattern from Paper II: SAM last-login (B), NIC LastWrite (D), event log session record (H) converge to corroborate session attribution.
Three-source convergence pattern: H corroborates D's network presence by recording the session in which network activity occurred.
Event logs (H) anchor execution telemetry (E) chronologically; H's logon session timestamps validate E's Prefetch timestamps.
NTFS metadata (I) provides structural ground truth for payload (C); MAC timestamps in $MFT validate semantic claims about file creation and modification.
I corroborates G: $MFT entries persist after deletion and validate RECYCLER chronology.
USN journal (J) confirms creation, modification, and deletion chronology for payload (C). Paper II walkthroughs cite $UsnJrnl as the precise timestamp source despite XP epoch parsing caveats.
J independently corroborates G: $UsnJrnl records deletion events with reason codes, validating RECYCLER's claim about what was deleted and when.
I (MFT) and J (USN journal) provide complementary structural views; J references MFT entries by record number.

convergence_patterns.name: Three-source session convergence
convergence_patterns.function: Paper II's defensible reconstruction standard: SAM last-login (B), NIC LastWrite (D), and event log session record (H) agreeing within 30 seconds corroborate session attribution and chronology. Confirmed against Pat Nov 16 (Nov 13 22:04Z) and Pat Nov 17 (Nov 17 02:27Z) in M57 investigations.

convergence_patterns.name: Payload lifecycle corroboration
convergence_patterns.function: User content (C) validated by NTFS metadata (I) and USN journal entries (J) to confirm creation, modification, and deletion chronology independent of semantic claims.
